newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-ZENDEN OFFERS NEW HOPE AS TAUMENT DEPARTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZENDEN OFFERS NEW HOPE AS TAUMENT DEPARTS.

text.p: With more star names about to abandon the Dutch league for the glamour of southern Europe, Feyenoord Rotterdam's clash with PSV Eindhoven on Sunday offers one departing talent an opportunity to bow out in glory and one new arrival the chance to seize centre stage.

For Feyenoord's right winger Gaston Taument, the match against PSV will be his last Dutch league classic. His speed and mazy dribbling attracted foreign bids and this year he settled a four-year contract starting this summer to play for Benfica.

His choice of the Portuguese club was the partly due to the similarities with Feyenoord, "Benfica is a people's club like Feyenoord with a lot of ambition, a large stadium and a lot of fans," he explained.

Despite his imminent departure, he remains a favourite with the Feyenoord crowd. He is very much a home-grown talent. He started with the club as a 17-year-old in 1988 and has since played 216 league matches, scoring 39 times.
His embarrassment of opposition full backs has earned him 15 Dutch caps, including a place in the squad for the 1994 World Cup finals in the United States.
Home fans will be eager to see a few last glimpses of magic.
Meanwhile, Boudewijn Zenden, the 20-year-old PSV winger, will hope to kick-start his promising career and hold down a regular place in the team, brushing off his super-sub tag.

Until the age of 16, he played both football and judo and, under the guidance of his father Pierre, a television judo commentator, he was three times judo champion of his home province of Limburg. The decision to settle for football was not easy.

"Judo is a very complete sport exercising all muscles. As you are on your own, it is also character building. The one-on-one contests are great, but I prefer the team spirit among soccer players," Zenden said.
PSV scouts spotted him playing in amateur leagues and he made his debut in August 1994 against Vitesse Arhem, replacing Peter Hoekstra for the last five minutes.
His arrival, however, created problems. PSV then had two left wingers, so one had to go.
Ajax expressed interest in the young talent, but PSV held firm. The result was the sale of Hoekstra to the Amsterdam club.
"The interest from both Ajax and PSV was flattering. I understood I was on the list of (Ajax coach Louis) van Gaal," Zenden said.
In 1994, PSV's then coach Kees Rijvers said Zenden was likely to outshine Ajax's highly regarded winger Marc Overmars.
However, he has found no permanent place under current boss Advocaat.

Zenden's forward runs show many flashes of brilliance, but he must concentrate more on defence to please the demanding Advocaat. With regular match appearances, Zenden may also impress foreign spies before his contract expires in two years time.
